criminal_definition: A person intentionally and repeatedly follows or harasses another person and makes a threat, expressed or implied, with intent to place the victim in reasonable fear of death or serious bodily injury.
criminal_penalty: First degree: Class C felony, 1 year and 1 day to 10 years; second degree (Ala. Code § 13A-6-90.1): Class B misdemeanor, up to 6 months; aggravated first degree: Class B felony, 2 to 20 years
cyber_note: Electronic stalking in the second degree covers placing an electronic tracking device on another person's property without consent or other lawful authorization.
order_duration: Permanent unless the court specifies otherwise or a later order modifies it
order_free_note: No filing fees, service fees, or subpoena costs in Protection from Abuse cases.
order_gap_note: The PFA order is only for a family/household member or current/former sexual/intimate partner — stalking is qualifying 'abuse' under Ala. Code § 30-5-2, but a stranger/neighbor/coworker stalker cannot get a PFA; remedy is criminal prosecution or a general civil injunction. No standalone non-family stalking order statute verified from an official source.
order_name: Protection Order under the Protection from Abuse Act
order_where: Circuit Court in the county where you live, where the defendant lives, where the abuse occurred, or where you are temporarily located to avoid abuse

coalition_name: Alaska Network on Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: A person knowingly engages in a course of conduct that recklessly places another person in fear of death or physical injury, or in fear of the death or physical injury of a family member.
criminal_penalty: Second degree: Class A misdemeanor, up to 1 year; first degree (with an aggravating factor such as violating a protective order, a victim under 16, or a deadly weapon): Class C felony, up to 5 years
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute found; AS 11.41.270 expressly includes electronic communications, GPS monitoring, and installing a device or software to observe or record a person as nonconsensual contact.
order_duration: 6 months unless earlier dissolved by the court
order_free_note: Filing fees may not be charged in any action seeking only the relief provided in AS 18.65.850-18.65.870.
order_name: Protective Order for Stalking and Sexual Assault
order_where: District or superior court; a parent or guardian may file on behalf of a minor

coalition_name: Arizona Coalition to End Sexual and Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person intentionally or knowingly engages in a course of conduct directed toward another person that causes the victim to suffer emotional distress or reasonably fear physical injury, property damage, or death.
criminal_penalty: Class 5 felony (emotional distress or fear of injury), 6 months to 2.5 years; Class 3 felony if the victim reasonably fears death, 2 to 8.75 years
cyber_note: Covers using an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten, or harass another person; stalking by electronic means is also charged under A.R.S. § 13-2923.
order_duration: 1 year after service on the defendant
order_free_note: A fee shall not be charged for filing a petition under this section.
order_where: Any magistrate, justice of the peace, or superior court judge in Arizona; any court in the state may issue or enforce it

criminal_definition: A person knowingly engages in a course of conduct that would place a reasonable person in the victim's position under emotional distress and in fear for his or her safety or a third person's safety.
criminal_penalty: First degree: Class C felony; second degree: Class D felony; third degree: Class A misdemeanor
cyber_note: Harassing communications covers using a telephone, mail, email, text message, social media, or any other electronic communication with the purpose of harassing, annoying, or alarming someone.
order_duration: 90 days to 10 years, at the court's discretion, and renewable
order_gap_note: The Order of Protection under the Domestic Abuse Act requires a family/household/dating relationship; no verified standalone non-family stalking protective order in Arkansas. A 2026 account confirms a judge could not issue one without that relationship.
order_name: Order of Protection under the Domestic Abuse Act of 1991
order_where: Circuit court; file with the circuit clerk in the county where the petitioner resides, where the alleged abuse occurred, or where the respondent may be served

coalition_name: California Partnership to End Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly follows or harasses another person and makes a credible threat with the intent to place that person in reasonable fear for his or her safety or the safety of his or her immediate family.
criminal_penalty: Wobbler: misdemeanor up to 1 year in county jail and/or a $1,000 fine; felony 2, 3, or 4 years in state prison if committed while a restraining order is in effect
cyber_note: Covers electronically distributing, publishing, or emailing another person's personal identifying information or a harassing message to incite unwanted physical contact, injury, or harassment by a third party; Penal Code § 646.9 also expressly includes threats made through an electronic communication device.
order_duration: Up to 5 years, renewable for another 5 years; defaults to 3 years if no expiration date is stated
order_free_note: No fee if the petition involves stalking, violence, or threats of violence; otherwise a filing fee applies.
order_where: Superior Court in the county where you live

criminal_definition: A person knowingly makes a credible threat and repeatedly follows, approaches, contacts, or places under surveillance another person, or repeatedly engages in conduct that would cause a reasonable person to suffer serious emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: First offense: Class 5 felony, 1 to 3 years (extraordinary risk, up to 4 years) and $1,000 to $100,000 fine; second offense within 7 years or while a protection order is in effect: Class 4 felony
cyber_note: Kiana Arellano's Law covers initiating electronic communication to harass or threaten bodily injury or property damage, or to make an obscene comment; repeated electronic conduct causing serious emotional distress can be charged as stalking under § 18-3-602.
order_duration: Temporary order until a hearing within 14 days; if granted, a permanent civil protection order
order_free_note: No filing fee may be assessed against a petitioner seeking protection as a victim of stalking, and no service fee may be assessed by a state or public agency.
order_where: Municipal court of record, county court, or district court in any county where the acts occurred, where a party resides, or where a party is employed

criminal_definition: A person knowingly engages in a course of conduct of two or more acts directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for his or her physical safety or the physical safety of a third person.
criminal_penalty: Second degree: Class A misdemeanor, up to 1 year and $2,000; first degree (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 53a-181c): Class D felony, 1 to 5 years and up to $5,000
cyber_note: Electronic stalking covers using electronic means to cause substantial emotional distress or reasonable fear of serious or fatal injury to the victim, a family member, or an intimate partner.
order_duration: Up to 1 year, extendable by the court on the applicant's motion
order_name: Civil Protection Order for a victim of sexual abuse, sexual assault, or stalking

criminal_definition: A person knowingly engages in a course of conduct of 3 or more separate incidents directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear physical injury to himself or herself or another person, or to suffer other significant mental anguish or distress.
criminal_penalty: Class G felony, up to 2 years; Class F felony if an aggravating factor applies; Class C felony if the person possesses a deadly weapon or causes serious physical injury, up to 15 years
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute found; harassment under 11 Del. C. § 1311 covers communicating by telephone, mail, or any other form of written or electronic communication in a manner likely to cause annoyance or alarm.
order_duration: Up to 3 years, renewable for up to 3 years
order_gap_note: The Sexual Violence Protective Order requires non-consensual sexual contact/penetration — stalking alone does not qualify. Stalking victims without a family/dating relationship would use a PFA only if they qualify, otherwise criminal prosecution.
order_where: Superior Court in the county where the petitioner resides, the respondent resides, or the alleged non-consensual sexual conduct occurred

coalition_name: Florida Partnership to End Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly follows, harasses, or cyberstalks another person, or makes a credible threat with the intent to place that person in reasonable fear for his or her safety.
criminal_penalty: Stalking or cyberstalking: first-degree misdemeanor, up to 1 year and $1,000; aggravated stalking: third-degree felony, up to 5 years
cyber_note: Cyberstalking is defined in the same statute as engaging in a pattern of electronic communication directed at a specific person that causes substantial emotional distress and serves no legitimate purpose.
order_duration: Final injunction remains in effect until modified or dissolved, with no automatic expiration date; temporary injunction up to 15 days
order_free_note: The clerk of court may not assess a filing fee for a petition for protection against stalking, and no bond is required.
order_where: Circuit court where the petitioner currently or temporarily resides, where the respondent resides, or where the stalking occurred

criminal_definition: A person follows, places under surveillance, or contacts another person at or about a place or places without the consent of the other person for the purpose of harassing and intimidating the other person.
criminal_penalty: First offense: misdemeanor, up to 12 months and $1,000; second or subsequent offense: felony, 1 to 10 years; aggravated stalking (O.C.G.A. § 16-5-91): felony, up to 10 years
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute found; O.C.G.A. § 16-5-90 covers broadcasting or publishing, including by electronic publication, a victim's picture, name, address, or phone number in violation of a court order.
order_duration: Temporary orders typically 6 to 12 months; the court may extend the order or convert it to a permanent order
order_free_note: There is no cost to file a petition for a protective order under Georgia's Family Violence Act.
order_where: Superior Court; file with the Clerk of Superior Court in the county where the respondent resides, or where the petitioner lives or the stalking occurred if the respondent lives outside Georgia
